executive_summary.conclusion: DuckDB clearly explains its analytical SQL role, open-source governance and current installation options. The observed obstacle is LTS Python installation continuity: the LTS documentation sends visitors back to the current release installer. Preserve the selected release in its installation link and show an LTS-specific command first. Twelve static pages, four rendered documents and four bounded searches support this assessment; sampled evidence includes extraction caps and eight collector HTTP 308 errors. Actual assistant citations, provider crawler access and behavioral outcomes were not measured.

not_checked: Actual assistant answers/citations and provider crawler IP access were not measured; no visibility score or probability is inferred.
Mobile layout, keyboard navigation, visible focus, contrast, performance metrics and behavioral analytics were not checked within the shared audit budget.
Eight HTTP 308 collection errors are retained in evidence.json. Browser and web tools reached the installation and announcement destinations; other affected routes were not individually followed.
Six static pages have evidence_truncated=true; no absence claim relies on their omitted content.
Published robots restrictions for old documentation versions are retained as scoped policy observations; owner intent and indexing of canonical destinations were not independently inspected.

Search locale and per-query ordering are unknown; the four-query tool response merged results. Independent governance certification, transaction completion and all client/version combinations were not checked.

readiness.detail: Robots returned 200 with Allow: / and restrictions on /docs/1.3, /docs/1.2, /docs/1.1, /docs/1.0 and /docs/0.10. Current and LTS task routes are allowed under the published wildcard rule for Googlebot, bingbot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot. Training and user-fetch roles were recorded separately; successful local GETs do not prove provider access. Eleven of twelve static pages have no observed indexing directive; /design is a noindex redirect stub with canonical /design/manual/, so the static candidate was not retained as a defect.

Landing-page source and rendered copy agree on analytical database identity, data formats and MIT/Foundation positioning. The static installation extraction lacks selected-client command content while the rendered Python selection supplies it; the homepage source and Python documentation provide supporting instructions, so this was not treated as a missing-answer defect. Some documentation evidence is capped. No material structured-data contradiction was established.

Four developer/data-analyst questions were frozen before supporting-page review and answered with inspected passages. This is task-specific answerability, not a prediction of assistant citations. The LTS-specific return-path problem is tracked separately as engagement friction.

Four exact searches dated 2026-09-08 are preserved in ledger.md. Opened DuckLabs announcement agrees with DuckDB on MIT licensing and Foundation stewardship, but DuckLabs is an affiliated first-party source. An independently authored arXiv paper dated 2026-03-03 reports a local DuckDB/Parquet deployment, supporting the product-use description only. No material contradiction or entity collision was observed in these opened sources; acquisition completion was not verified.

Own desktop in-app browser tab rendered the homepage, installer, current Python overview and LTS Python overview. Both Python/version choices have visible controls. Current Python installation and documentation journey completed; the LTS return link loses the selected version. No blocking overlay was observed in the inspected states; accessibility conformance was not tested.

findings.title: LTS Python documentation resets the chosen installation version

evidence.observation: Rendered journey: selecting 1.4.5 (LTS) at /install/?environment=python&platform=macos&version=lts displays 'pip install duckdb==1.4.5' and links to /docs/lts/clients/python/overview.html. That destination visibly identifies '1.4 LTS' but its Installation section shows 'pip install duckdb' and links to /install/?environment=python. Clicking that link reaches /install/?environment=python&platform=macos with 1.5.5 (current) selected and the unpinned command. One affected LTS return path among two Python release-context paths checked; current-release path works.

suggested_action.summary: In the LTS Python overview, append version=lts to the installation link and present an explicitly LTS-pinned package command; label any current-release alternative.
suggested_action.mechanism: Keeps the release choice the website already knows attached to the installation instructions, reducing the chance of installing a different release line.
suggested_action.verification: Select Python and 1.4.5 LTS, follow Client documentation page, then its installation page link; the installer must still select LTS and display the LTS-pinned command. Confirm the ordinary current-release path still selects current. No installation is required for this check.
